mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the permission-matrix definition lets Alloy invent a matrix in which Customer -> DecideApp is allowed. The injected fact forces such a customer-decide operation to succeed, which violates the documented allow/deny grid (PermissionCompleteness), the least-privilege guard (LeastPrivilege), and the staff-only decision rule (FR_015).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrix { some op: Operation, u: User | u.role = Customer and op.caller = u and op.kind = DecideApp and op.outcome = OpAllowed and some op.authenticated }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the lifecycle-audit fact lets Alloy build an application with no submission audit entry, with a forged decision entry whose state is inconsistent, and with the wrong actor. The injection forces an application whose submission event is missing, immediately violating AuditCompleteness and FR_016.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditLifecycle { some a: LoanApplication | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.application = a and ae.eventType = EvSubmitted }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the one-decision-per-application coupling lets two Decision rows attach to the same application — exactly the concurrent-double-decision race that FR-012 forbids and FR-011 (immutability) rules out.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DecisionCoupling { some a: LoanApplication, disj d1, d2: Decision | d1.application = a and d2.application = a }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the partial-unique-index analogue lets a single customer have two applications simultaneously in Pending Review, which FR-005 forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OnePending { some u: User | u.role = Customer and (some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.customer = u and a2.customer = u and a1.status = PendingReview and a2.status = PendingReview) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the auth-semantics fact unties outcome from authentication, matrix, and ownership. The injection forces an unauthenticated customer to succeed at viewing a non-owned application, breaking the auth gate, ownership-based access, and FR-013 ownership scoping.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthSemantics { some op: Operation, u: User, a: LoanApplication | u.role = Customer and op.caller = u and op.kind = ViewApp and op.target = a and a.customer != u and no op.authenticated and op.outcome = OpAllowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing response semantics lets the externally visible status code drift. The injection forces a customer probing someone else's application to receive 403 Forbidden — which leaks existence, the exact failure FR-013 / SC-004 forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ResponseLeak { some op: Operation, u: User, a: LoanApplication | u.role = Customer and op.caller = u and op.kind = ViewApp and op.target = a and a.customer != u and some op.authenticated and op.response = ForbiddenResponse }
